subject: Model shortlist & capacity check — NexaHealth onboarding
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nexamed.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: NexaHealth Procurement <procurement@nexamed.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Model shortlist & capacity check — NexaHealth onboarding

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team here is excited to move forward with Redwood for our clinical summarization flow. Before we kick off the pilot, procurement asked us to double-check the recommended model shortlist against our expected workload so we can lock budget and the initial reserved capacity.

Quick context:
- Primary use: generate 1–2 paragraph clinical summaries from the last 12 months of notes (HTML -> plain text -> summarize).
- Typical context window: ~6k tokens (we strip templates, but some records reach 7.5k).
- Expected volume: ~250k generated tokens/month in month 1, ramp to ~1.2M by month 6.
- Peak pattern: daily peaks at 300–450 requests/hour across ~20 concurrent users during batch processing windows (06:00–09:00 PST).
- Latency target: p95 < 200ms for interactive flows; batch can be >1s.

Attached is our sizing worksheet (Nexa_Sizing_Sheet.xlsx) and a short sample of the heavier notes. Can you confirm: 1) a model shortlist that fits the context length and latency targets, 2) rough per-token cost guidance for hosted vs. dedicated, and 3) any recommendations for prefix caching or batching given our peak rhythms?

We'd like to have a mutually agreed action plan by end of next week so procurement can prepare the initial PO.

Best,
Elena Soto
Director, Product
NexaHealth


From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nexamed.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Model shortlist & capacity check — NexaHealth onboarding

Elena — thanks for the context and the sizing sheet. I looped in Monica (CS lead) and Ben (solutions/infra) to validate the shortlist and capacity plan. High level answers below; more detailed notes and a proposed next steps list follow.

Shortlist (recommend initial A/B):
- redwood/8k-guardrail-v1 (8k context, low-latency tuned; good for clinical fidelity)
- openfactor-7b-q4 (cost-efficient option; good perf with quantization but expect slightly higher tail latency under load)
- rw-medium-16k (if you want headroom for edge cases >8k; more costly but reduces truncation risk)

Rationale: the first option matches your stated ~6k typical with buffer to 8k; openfactor is lower cost for non-critical summaries; rw-medium-16k only if you plan to keep full 12-month context in a single prompt (otherwise we recommend prefixing + KV cache).

Cost guidance (very rough):
- Hosted API: expect ~$0.0018–0.0035 per generated token depending on model and caching.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): blended unit cost can be ~30–50% lower at steady state with a 6–12 month commit (depends on instance family).

Quick infra recs: prefix cache for repetitive metadata (patient templates), continuous batching during batch windows, and an autoscale policy that favors small burst capacity for the 06:00–09:00 PST window.

Next steps I propose:
1) Monica to validate monthly token estimates and provide a run-rate table by model.
2) Ben to map concurrency -> slot sizing and recommend a Dedicated vs Hosted delta for month 1 and month 6.
3) Quick QA plan: 3-day A/B pilot with 500 representative requests (we can run on hosted).

Can we set a brief call tomorrow (30m) to align on the run-rate assumptions? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference


From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Elena Soto <elena.soto@nexamed.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Model shortlist & capacity check — NexaHealth onboarding

Thanks Kim + Elena — I went through the attached sizing sheet and ran a quick token breakdown. Notes below and I attached a one-page run-rate table to the Drive link (also pasted key rows here).

Assumptions I used (conservative):
- Avg input tokens per request: 1,800 (post-cleaning)
- Avg generated tokens per summary: 220
- Monthly active requests M1: 1,000 (scattered across days); ramp to 5,000 by M6

Estimated generated tokens/month by model (sample):
- redwood/8k-guardrail-v1: M1 = 220k gen tokens, M6 = 1.1M gen tokens
- openfactor-7b-q4: M1 = 220k gen tokens, M6 = 1.1M gen tokens (same gen tokens — cost differs)

Peak concurrency / slot sizing suggestion (back-of-envelope):
- For p95 ~200ms: 20 slots of redwood/8k should cover 20 concurrent interactive users with headroom for bursts (assuming 1 request at a time per user).
- Batch window (06:00–09:00 PST): recommend an autoscale policy to add +10 slots during that window for faster throughput.

Caching / truncation:
- We recommend a two-stage prompt: 1) prefix cache for patient metadata/standard headers (reduces avg input tokens by ~15–25%), 2) rolling context for long timelines (if you need >8k, stitch via retrieval + short context rather than full 12-month dump).

Drive summary: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1nexa-sprint-plan (one-pager + run-rate table).

Attachments referenced: Nexa_Sizing_Sheet.xlsx (from customer), our internal run-rate table (nexa_runrate_m1_m6.csv).

Happy to take this to a short pilot plan — if we agree the models, Ben can draft the slot-level sizing and I will coordinate the 3-day A/B pilot test data.

— Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference


From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, Elena Soto <elena.soto@nexamed.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 08:11:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Model shortlist & capacity check — NexaHealth onboarding

Quick follow up on sizing from infra/solutions side. Monica's numbers look reasonable — a couple clarifying Qs so we can produce a slot-level commit recommendation: 
1) Can you confirm whether interactive users will make concurrent requests during the batch window, or if batch processing is separate automated jobs? If separate, we can schedule dedicated batch nodes to avoid impacting interactive tail latency.
2) Do you have an expected SLA for time-to-result during the 06:00–09:00 window (e.g., max 1.5s)?

Prelim slot mapping (draft):
- redwood/8k-guardrail-v1: 20 production slots (interactive), 10 batch slots (autoscale) => equates to ~2 x m60-like instances if on dedicated pools (rough ballpark).
- openfactor-7b-q4: same slot counts but fewer tokens/sec per slot under quantized exec; add +20% slots to match throughput.

I attached a sample load CSV (nexa_load_profile.csv) mirroring the M1 peak pattern — I can run a sim against our dev fleet to validate p95.

If Elena confirms batch separation and a 1.5s target for batch, we can recommend a small Dedicated pilot for month 1 (to satisfy procurement) with autoscale back to Hosted for month 6 if you prefer lower committed spend. I'll put numbers in a short spreadsheet and share.

— Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference


From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nexamed.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Model shortlist & capacity check — NexaHealth onboarding

Thanks — this is exactly what procurement wanted to see. A few quick answers:
- Batch processing is separate (we run nightly aggregation jobs that hit the summarization endpoint in bulk). Interactive clinicians will not typically run during the batch window.
- Batch SLA: <= 2s acceptable, interactive p95 < 200ms preferred.

We're happy to start with a small Dedicated pilot for M1. Please send a mutual action plan with these milestones:
1) Pilot environment & test dataset provisioned (by Dec 8)
2) 3-day A/B pilot run (Dec 9–11)
3) Procurement signs PO for M1 Dedicated (Dec 15)

If you can get a mutual action plan (with dates and owners) in the next 24 hours, procurement will prepare the PO.

Elena
Director, Product — NexaHealth
